Let
\[
Y=12-2S.
\]
After symmetrizing the law under \(S\mapsto 12-S\), which preserves all constraints and the objective, put
\[
r_d=P(|S-6|=d),\qquad d=0,1,\dots,6.
\]
Then \(|Y|=2d\). Since the variables are six-wise independent and unbiased, the first six moments of \(Y\) match those of a sum of \(12\) independent Rademacher variables. Hence
\[
\sum r_d=1,\qquad \sum r_d d^2=3,\qquad \sum r_d d^4=\frac{51}{2},\qquad \sum r_d d^6=\frac{681}{2}.
\]
The quantity to maximize is
\[
r_6+\lambda r_5.
\]

For \(0\le \lambda\le \frac{175}{648}\), use
\[
P(u)=\frac{u(u-4)(u-9)}{31104}.
\]
For \(u=d^2\in\{0,1,4,9,16,25,36\}\), this satisfies
\[
P(36)=1,\qquad P(25)=\frac{175}{648},\qquad P(u)\ge 0\text{ otherwise}.
\]
Thus \(P(d^2)\ge \mathbf 1_{d=6}+\lambda \mathbf 1_{d=5}\), so
\[
r_6+\lambda r_5\le E[P(d^2)]
=\frac{1}{31104}\left(\frac{681}{2}-13\cdot\frac{51}{2}+36\cdot 3\right)
=\frac{13}{3456}.
\]
Equality is attained by
\[
(r_0,r_2,r_3,r_6)=\left(\frac{77}{144},\frac{33}{128},\frac{11}{54},\frac{13}{3456}\right),
\]
all other \(r_d=0\).

For \(\lambda\ge \frac{175}{648}\), use
\[
Q(u)=\frac{u(u-4)(u-9)}{8400}.
\]
Then \(Q(25)=1\), \(Q(36)=\frac{648}{175}\), and \(Q(u)\ge0\) on the same seven points. Since \(\lambda\ge 175/648\),
\[
\lambda Q(d^2)\ge \mathbf 1_{d=6}+\lambda \mathbf 1_{d=5}.
\]
Therefore
\[
r_6+\lambda r_5\le \lambda E[Q(d^2)]
=\lambda\cdot \frac{39}{2800}.
\]
Equality is attained by
\[
(r_0,r_2,r_3,r_5)=\left(\frac{99}{200},\frac{99}{280},\frac{11}{80},\frac{39}{2800}\right),
\]
all other \(r_d=0\).

These extremal \(r_d\) distributions are realized by choosing \(S=6\pm d\) symmetrically and then choosing uniformly among binary strings of Hamming weight \(S\). The moment identities above give mutual independence for every subfamily of size at most six.

Thus the maximum is
\[
\boxed{
\max\left\{\frac{13}{3456},\frac{39\lambda}{2800}\right\}
}
\]
equivalently, \(\frac{13}{3456}\) for \(0\le\lambda\le\frac{175}{648}\), and \(\frac{39\lambda}{2800}\) for \(\lambda\ge\frac{175}{648}\).
